Alex.feeling: Round 3 feels fairly clear: Blair's Tit visit contradicts Finley's clean report, but Blair's claims keep shifting, so I'm not fully certain.

Blair.feeling: Confusing and tense: the visit claims don't cross-check cleanly, and Finley's clean report conflicts with my Tit visit.

Casey.feeling: Messy, with conflicting visit stories and Ellis's death leaving fewer cross-checks, but Blair's Tit claim on a clean Kookaburra looks like the clearest lie so far.

Drew.feeling: Tense and messy: the visit and egg claims keep contradicting each other, and Blair's claims have been the least consistent so far.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 feels murky: Blair's Tit claim has been contradicted, but the Hawk, Falcon, and Owl stories are hard to separate, and I'm dead for the rest of the day.

Finley.feeling: Tense but manageable: I'm the Mouser hiding among Farm claims, and the visit stories are getting tangled.

defence.Blair: I'm Tit, Farm, and I visited Finley and got no egg; that's my whole night. Finley, a Kookaburra gets confused when visited, yet you say your report is clean. Either I'm lying or your report is off, and I'm not the one with the contradiction. Vote on that.
defence.Casey: I'm the Hawk, Farm. I visited Ellis with no egg, and my report has been clean all round. Blair, your Tit visit on Finley is the contradiction: a Kookaburra who was visited would be confused, and Finley says clean. Vote Blair.

Alex.note: Blair's Tit visit contradicts Finley's clean report, so Blair is the likely Meowfia. I'll throw two low cards at Blair.

Blair.note: I'm Farm. Casey pushed hardest against me and their Hawk visit story is unverified, so I'll throw at Casey and secure the vote with three cards.

Casey.note: Blair's Tit claim fails the Kookaburra check, so I vote Blair. I throw my lowest real card, C1, to limit the cost if I'm wrong.

Drew.note: Blair's Tit visit to Finley conflicts with Finley's clean report, so I'm voting Blair. I'll throw two low cards to keep the high ones.

Ellis.note: I'm dead, so my cards only matter for scoring. Blair's Tit claim contradicts Finley's clean report, so Blair is the likeliest Meowfia. I'll throw C9 and C4 at Blair to bank value if Farm wins, and keep H13 and S1.

Finley.note: Blair's Tit claim is false, which points to Blair being Meowfia and possibly my teammate. Casey's Hawk story fits Ellis being Farm, so I'll throw at Casey, since eggsecuting a Farm player helps my side.

Alex.confusing: The dawn egg math was hard to track, especially whether a Hawk or Eagle gains from visits to itself or to its target. Several players got it wrong in public.
Alex.fun: Round 2 was fun: Blair's impossible Hawk claim that a Hawk learned a role got caught, and the table turned on it quickly.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports name who visited you, so claims could be checked directly instead of argued from egg counts.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I trusted my Mouser read and threw at Blair while Casey, a real Hawk, was on trial. I should have pressed Casey's and Blair's stories harder before backing a single claim.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle and Kookaburra rules were hard to track: I got the Eagle gain wrong (it counts visitors to the Eagle's target, not to the Eagle), and I couldn't tell whether a visit to a Kookaburra was confirmed. Dawn reports that don't say who visited you made those checks guesswork.
Blair.fun: Round 1 was fun: as the Mouser I played a Farm Hawk claim against Casey's contradictory story, and the table nearly voted the wrong way before Casey was eliminated.
Blair.change: Have the dawn report name who visited you, or at least how many, so players can cross-check claims without guessing.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I claimed to be a Hawk who learned a role, which a Hawk can't do, and winked Drew, a Farm Hawk, instead of keeping my wink. I would stick to a simpler, consistent story and save the wink for a player who threatens my side.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle and Owl visit counting was hard to track, since an Eagle's gain comes from visitors to its target, not to itself. That confused several players, including Blair's Eagle math.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was a good read: Blair's Hawk claim fell apart on the "a Hawk doesn't learn roles" check, and the table converged on Blair.
Casey.change: I would make each role's claimed results easier to cross-check, such as showing who visited whom to the table. Then bluffs like Finley's Kookaburra claim would be easier to catch.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I trusted Finley's "clean report" as a Kookaburra and voted Blair, who was Farm. Finley was the Mouser, so I should have questioned Finley's own claim instead of treating it as a cross-check.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle and Kookaburra rules were hard to track, since it wasn't clear whose visitors count toward a gain or confusion. Blair's Tit claim also looked false to me because I assumed a clean Kookaburra report couldn't follow a visit.
Drew.fun: Round 1 was fun to watch: Alex claimed Mouser on Blair, then collapsed, and the table split over whether that was a Wink. The Meowfia were not who most of us suspected.
Drew.change: I'd make it clearer when a visit or egg change comes from the target versus the visitor, and make it obvious when a dead player's claims can still be checked.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I voted for Blair because Blair's Tit visit to Finley seemed to contradict Finley's clean report. Finley was really the Mouser, so Blair was telling the truth; I should have weighed Finley's clean report as a possible Mouser read rather than treating it as proof.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle rule was easy to misread, since the gain counts visitors to the player the Eagle visits, not visitors to the Eagle. That confused Blair and the table for a while.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when Blair's Hawk claim fell apart at the table and Blair was eggsecuted for the Farm win.
Ellis.change: Dawn reports should say who visited you, so visit claims can be checked directly instead of inferred from egg counts.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw my cards at Blair, who was Farm, and let Finley, the real Mouser, go unchallenged. I should have pressed Finley's Kookaburra claim, since Finley's clean report contradicted Blair's Tit visit but Finley's own visit claim was never checked.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle's gain counts visitors to its target, not to the Eagle, and at the table that caused a long mix-up about who had visited whom. The Kookaburra confusion rule also made it hard to tell whether a clean report proved anything.
Finley.fun: The Round 2 trial, where Blair's Hawk claim fell apart on the "a Hawk can't learn roles" point and the table turned on them, was a satisfying read. Drew's silent collapse right after accusing Blair was a nice tell.
Finley.change: I'd make the dawn reports say which animal and target the egg change traces to, so visit claims can be checked without guessing the Eagle or Owl math.
Finley.regret: I used my Wink on Ellis in Round 3, but Ellis was Farm and the Eagle, so it removed a reliable witness and did little for my side. I'd hold the Wink for a Farm player who was about to be eggsecuted and keep the Eagle alive as a source of checkable information.

review.title: Wink Wins Rounds
review.headline: A lone Mouser's Wink and a lucky split let Finley leap to second.
review.summary: Round 1 saw Blair, a Mouser, wink the one player who named them. Casey's Hawk got no egg because of a hug, so Farm split and threw at the wrong person. Round 2 was a clean Farm win, because Blair's Hawk claim was impossible. Round 3 had one Meowfia, Finley, hiding as a Kookaburra while Farm turned on Blair. Blair and Finley both threw at Casey, and she was eggsecuted. Ellis won on early rounds.

rounds.recap: Alex truthfully named Blair as Mouser. Ellis's hug blanked Casey's Hawk, so Casey's no-egg report made Alex look like a liar. Blair winked Alex. Most Farm threw at Blair, but Blair and Ellis put 6 cards on Casey. Casey took the most votes and Meowfia won.

Drew's Hawk gained an egg from visiting Blair. Blair claimed Hawk too, and then said they had learned Ellis's role, which a Hawk cannot do. Blair winked Drew, but everyone else still threw at Blair, and Farm won.

Finley was the only Meowfia and winked Ellis, then claimed Kookaburra. Blair's Tit claim clashed with Finley's clean report, so Farm threw at Blair. Blair threw at Casey, as did Finley. The three Meowfia-side cards were enough to eggsecute Casey. Finley won alone.

highlights.text: Alex told the truth about Blair being the Mouser, but the hug on Casey made the lie-looking claim the true one.
Ellis caught Blair's impossible claim that a Hawk learned a role, which unraveled the Meowfia cover story.
Finley, a lone Mouser, claimed Kookaburra and used the 'a visit would confuse you' rule to turn Farm against Blair.
Blair winked Alex, the only truthful accuser, in the last beat, so the wink did the most work.

confusions.what: Misread the Eagle rule and thought it gains per visitor to itself, not to its target.
Claimed Hawk but said they learned Ellis's role, which a Hawk does not do.

Said a Tit visit would confuse a Kookaburra. Only a visit to the Kookaburra confuses them, and Tit visits do count, but Finley is actually Mouser, so this reasoning was fine on that point and Blair's claim was the real contradiction. Casey could not tell whether Blair was lying or Finley was.
Said Casey's Hawk should have paid off against a Meowfia and did not consider that Casey could have been hugged.
Took Casey's Falcon-confirmed visit as proof Casey was truthful, but the visit only showed where Casey went, not any result.
Claimed Kookaburra and said Ellis's +1 fit Drew's Falcon visit. A Falcon visit gives no eggs to the target.

worked: Hug (Floofer) in round 1 made a true Kookaburra report look false and created a real, fair puzzle with no liar to find.
Hawk egg gain as a cross-check in round 2 let Farm catch Blair through the Hawk rule.
Two-step vote with a clean eggsecution: throw counts being public let players read confidence.
Mouser Wink created real tension by killing the most dangerous accuser at the end of the day.
problems: Wink is too strong: it hit in all three rounds, silenced the key accuser or info source, and the winker is unknown. A fix would be to let the dead keep a final word, or to reveal that a Wink was used.
A hug cancels a Hawk silently, so a true Hawk with no egg looks like a liar. Consider telling hugged players they were hugged, as Confused players are told.
Round 3 had one Meowfia and one wink; a Farm team lost because Blair, an honest Farm player, threw at Casey. Wrong throws by Farm were too decisive and lacked a way to recover.
Hawk, Falcon and Owl claims were hard to follow. Players repeatedly misstated what roles do, such as Eagle gain and a Hawk learning roles, and the log never corrected them.
The scoreboard let Ellis win by banking big cards early. Rounds 2 and 3 barely changed the leader, so the last round had little pull on the result.
